log: CAN REASONING FIND THE MISSING PIECE WHERE COUNTING CANNOT?
Six hand-built signals and an 8,929-parameter set transformer all land on recall@1 ~0.37 against
a 0.498 ceiling. Every one of them sees candidates only as graph statistics and none of them
knows what the reaction DOES. This arm is given the chemistry and nothing else.
CAVEAT DECLARED FIRST: these are curated reactions published before the training cutoff, so a
high score is partly recall of the literature the answer key was built from, NOT discovery.
It is still a valid CEILING PROBE, and results are stratified by catalyst fame to measure how
much of any advantage is memorisation.
PREDECLARED: tie ~ 0.367 => the tie group is underdetermined and the ceiling is unreachable.
tie >> 0.367 => the feature arms lacked reaction semantics, not capacity. open >> tie =>
the bottleneck is retrieval, not ordering.

READING
CONTROL FIRST. The scrambled arm saw the SAME candidate lists attached to the WRONG reaction
and scored 0.320; the honest arm scored 0.435 (paired p=0.0000).
The reaction text IS doing work: +0.115 over the same lists with the wrong chemistry.
So the honest arm is reading the reaction, not just picking the most familiar-looking gene.
REASONING BEATS COUNTING. 0.435 against freq 0.355, paired p=0.0052, against a
0.505 ceiling -- 66% of the headroom where six hand-built signals and a transformer claimed ~30%.
What the feature arms lacked was reaction semantics, not capacity.
BUT NOT ESTABLISHED AGAINST THE STRONGEST BASELINE: set_transformer reaches 0.395
and the paired test cannot separate it from 0.435 (p=0.1686). At n=200 the
honest claim is 'beats frequency counting', not 'beats everything'.
CONTAMINATION: the gain over freq is +0.099 on network-RARE catalysts and +0.061
on network-famous ones -- LARGER where the enzyme is rarer, which is the opposite of what
pure memorisation of famous enzymes would produce.
Read that with care in BOTH directions: 'rare' here means the catalyst runs few OTHER reactions
in this network, which is not the same as rare in the literature. A one-reaction enzyme can still
be a textbook enzyme, so this bounds the contamination loosely rather than ruling it out.
OPEN-ENDED, no candidate list: 0.720. The list-constrained ceiling is 0.505, so the
reasoning arm names the right enzyme MORE often with no list than any arm can achieve with
one (0.720 vs 0.505). The candidate list is a CEILING, not a help: the chemistry-
neighbour retrieval step is what limits this problem, and ranking work cannot fix it.
CLEANEST COMPARISON -- 137 puzzles with 2+ candidates AND no answer named in the
reaction: freq 0.292 vs closed-book reasoning 0.423 (+0.131).
OUT OF 10: freq gets 3.5, the transformer 4.0, closed-book reasoning 4.3 on the same task,
and 7.2 with no candidate list at all. Perfect tie-breaking would get 5.0.
